extracted.intended_audience: artists, art historians, conservators, and readers of Vasari's Lives
extracted.subtask_description: Implicit production and evaluative principles for painting and sculpture drawn from a biographical/historical account of Buonamico Buffalmacco (early Renaissance). Emphasizes techniques, materials, compositional invention, and factors affecting longevity and expressive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid purple ground if longevity desired
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘to make a ground of purple, which in time produces a salt that becomes corroded and eats away the white and other colours ... it is no marvel if this work is spoilt and eaten away’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: using a purple ground that later forms salts and corrodes overlying paint. Explicit advice: 'This method of working should be used by no one who is anxious that his pictures should have long life.' Example: Buffalmacco's flesh-colours were later lost leaving only the purple.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execute fresco on fresh plaster (buon fresco) for durability
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘these works ... were wrought purely on the fresh plaster... the water which has rained over them for so many years has not been able to spoil them or to prevent their excellence from being recognized’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production guideline: apply pigments to fresh (wet) plaster to lock colours into the substrate; this technique increases longevity and resistance to weathering. Example: Buffalmacco's frescoes on fresh plaster survived much better than those on corroding grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey vivid emotions through faces and gestures
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages praise scenes where 'nurses and mothers ... seeking all the assistance ... their nails, their teeth, and every movement of the body, there is shown ... rage and fury than of woe' and other scenes where 'fear of death and the grief and terror' are well expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative criterion: lifelike, emotionally charged expressions and bodily gestures increase the effectiveness of narrative scenes. Examples: Massacre of the Innocents, martyrdom scenes, Judas hanging — praised for natural, moving emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivacity and well-conceived attitudes in figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Works are commended for 'vivacity in the figures, good skill and loveliness in the colouring, and signs ... that the hand ... could very well express the conceptions of his mind' and for 'well-conceived attitudes' in boat figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compositional guideline: figures should show natural, lively postures and be well-arranged to convey narrative and beauty. This is a marker of skill even if drawing power is modest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention and judgement (originality + sound design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several works are praised as 'executed with invention and judgment' and that Buonamico's 'design and invention' could be used profitably by later artists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative principle: originality of idea (invention) combined with sound compositional choices (judgment) distinguishes superior works. Diligence amplifies these qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence and taking pains produce superior results
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘when he thought fit to use diligence and to take pains, which rarely came to pass, he was not inferior to any painter whatsoever of his times.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production/value rule: careful, painstaking effort yields high-quality work; slovenliness undermines potential. Examples contrast sporadic diligence producing excellent frescoes with otherwise careless habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polish marble to achieve softness and lifelike quality
rubrics_metrics.description: On Nino Pisano's marble Madonnas: 'Nino was beginning to rob the stone of its hardness and to reduce it to the softness of flesh, giving it lustre by means of the highest polish.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sculptural technique: high polish on marble can produce flesh-like softness and lustre, enhancing realism. Use of polish is a deliberate tool to transform material qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate binders/mediums for permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: A painted child was transformed into a 'little bear, but in colours made only with water, without size or distemper' and later removed with a wet sponge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical guidance: using water-only paints without proper sizing or binding makes paint ephemeral and easily removed. For permanence use proper distemper/tempera binders or fresco technique as appropriate. The anecdote illustrates how removable water-paint is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not judge artists by outward appearance; judge work itself
rubrics_metrics.description: Anecdote: Buffalmacco disguised a pitcher as a master; the nuns were deceived by clothes until they saw the actual work. 'it is not always by their clothes that the works of men should be judged.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curatorial/evaluative ethic: assess artistic merit on the quality of work rather than social status, dress, or external markers of respectability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorative relief, gilding, and added ornament can enhance prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of raised diadems and gilded ornaments is mentioned (e.g., a diadem in plaster, gold diadems, ornamental frames added to Madonnas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production note: adding relief work, gilding, and ornamental frames was a period practice to increase visual richness and perceived value; but such applications can be playful (roaches crown) or carry social/political implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompany pictorial narratives with explanatory inscriptions when helpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Buonamico wrote a long sonnet in capital letters under his depiction of God and the heavens 'to explain his story with verses similar to the pictures of that age.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicative guideline: textual captions or poems may be used to clarify complex iconography for contemporary viewers; this was an accepted practice in the period and may aid interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include portraits and contemporary likenesses for relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Several works include portraits (e.g., 'the head of the latter being a portrait of Andrea from the life', 'portrait of Pope Alexander IV').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compositional/practical advice: incorporating recognizable portraits can provide historical reference, patronage signaling, or local relevance; it was a common device in period narrative cycles.
